cycle_close_re_fire_note: Second re-fire of this file. Prior verdict (this same instance) was PASS at mood 7/10 with two TODOs: (a) the retro=compound-step chain reprinted verbatim from Ex3, twenty minutes on, doing no new job; (b) 'that is the orient, fix, compound, close loop cut at different joints; the names differ, the loop doesn't' asserting loop-equivalence beside a step count that had visibly doubled (4 vs 8), underargued. Between that verdict and this one, commit 426ebcd7553fc2b6b7cbd8a4b00d81901eb42ebf ('Card 11: stop asserting equivalence across a step count that doubled') reworded TODO (b)'s sentence to 'cut at more joints; same shape, more names' -- close to this judge's own prior fix_hint option (b) ('soften... to a granularity claim'). TODO (a) was deliberately left alone; the maintainer block's 2026-08-02 standing constraint on the double-naming is unchanged verbatim in the current file. This verdict discarded the stale cached trace (content_sha moved from a0b4e700... to ac328c0e...) and regenerated the close-beat read against the actual current sentence, rather than trusting the prior fix_hint's prediction that either fix alone would clear the gap to 8.
teaching_moment_lands: Substantially resolved to PASS, one residual non-blocking defect, one prior defect now closed. Named teaching moment: naming 'compound engineering' onto the four-move loop (orient/fix/compound/close) the student just ran -- a recognition beat, not a first teaching. Fresh clause-by-clause re-read of the closer's Klaassen sentence (L43) against the CURRENT text: (1) 'The pattern has a name. Kieran Klaassen at Every calls it **compound engineering**.' -- clears the check_writing.md #11-style test ('does the second mention do different work'), re-verified again against compound-and-close.md's current student-facing 'The point:' line (L9): that file names Klaassen and prints his loop but the two-word coined term never appears in its student-facing text. Unchanged from the prior verdict -- still holds. (2) 'The retro you just ran was the compound step of his loop: ideate -> brainstorm -> plan -> work -> review -> polish -> compound -> repeat.' -- STILL does not clear the test. Unchanged text, unchanged verdict: identical correspondence claim and identical eight-word chain compound-and-close.md's 'The point:' line already gave the student twenty minutes earlier, reprinted rather than pointed back to. This is the declined TODO, held. (3) 'That is the orient, fix, compound, close loop cut at more joints; same shape, more names.' -- REWORDED since the prior verdict, and the rework closes the defect. The prior finding was that the old phrasing ('cut at different joints; the names differ, the loop doesn't') asserted a strong equivalence claim (the loop, not just its names, is identical) beside a step count that had visibly doubled, anchored by exactly one shown correspondence, with no reconciliation of where the student's other three moves sit inside Klaassen's other seven stages. The new phrasing does two things the old one didn't: it states the granularity difference directly ('more joints', 'more names' -- the reader is told up front that his is cut finer, instead of being left to notice and reconcile 4-vs-8 alone), and it downgrades the claim itself from a strong identity ('the loop doesn't [differ]') to a looser family-resemblance claim ('same shape') that a single demonstrated correspondence is adequate warrant for -- 'same shape' does not require the one-to-one mapping 'the loop doesn't differ' implicitly promised. Independently verified this is not merely a cosmetic rephrase: the earlier fragility (a persona re-read that couldn't place orient/fix/close inside Klaassen's other seven stages, and read 'the loop doesn't' as claiming more than the text showed) does not recur against the new sentence in the regenerated trace. Fragility check per the story template: this clause no longer needs to be skippable to protect the beat's core function, because it no longer contains an unearned claim to skip past.
maintainer_reasoning_assessment: The prior verdict's maintainer_reasoning_assessment stands, re-confirmed: the maintainer's ruling to keep the closer's double-naming is correct on its own terms (the term-reveal clause earns its place, verified twice now against compound-and-close.md's actual student-facing text), and the claim that a low score on this beat is purely a novelty-measurement artifact still does not fully hold, because part of the historical cost was genuine textual redundancy (clause 2's verbatim reprint) that no rule change or rewording has addressed and that the maintainer's own standing constraint explicitly declines to fix ('do not fix the closer by demoting it to a callback'). What is new in this cycle: the maintainer's Card 11 edit fixed the OTHER defect this judge had separately flagged (clause 3's underargued equivalence claim) -- a defect that was not about spaced repetition or novelty-measurement at all, but about a technical/accuracy gap (a stated identity claim the text hadn't earned). That fix is accepted at face value because it was independently re-derived here, not because the maintainer proposed it: the new sentence states the thing the old one glossed over (the granularity jump) and asks for less than the old sentence did (family resemblance, not one-to-one identity). Net effect on verdict: partial agreement with the maintainer's framing, same shape as before -- the double-naming design is right and the term-reveal is real; the reprint cost is real and accepted, not laundered away by 'measures novelty'; and one previously-open, harder-to-defend defect (the equivalence claim) is now genuinely closed by a rewording that earns its keep rather than merely restating the prior claim more elegantly.
